### AI Policy

| Aspect | Detail |
|--------|--------|
| **Has journal-specific AI policy?** | *(see summary — defaults to publisher-level policy unless a journal-specific override was found)* |
| **Explicit permission gate?** | conditional |
| **Leniency (1-5)** | 3 |
| **Summary** | Publisher-wide policy (not journal-specific): generative AI cannot be listed as author (fails ICMJE criteria). Text-generation use is permitted but must be disclosed in Acknowledgements (and Methods if applicable), naming tool/version/model. Authors remain fully responsible for factual accuracy and plagiarism checks of AI-assisted content. AI-generated figures/images/illustrations are explicitly prohibited. Optional: authors encouraged (not required) to upload prompts/outputs as supplementary material. No evidence this journal has a stricter section-specific addendum beyond the site-wide policy. |
| **Source URL** | https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/policies-and-publication-ethics |

### Preprint Policy

> AI-research note (not broken down per-stage): Yes. Preprinting before or during review is permitted provided the preprint server imposes no restrictions on copyright/reuse; the preprint must be cited/acknowledged in the submitted manuscript. Frontiers has direct submission integrations with bioRxiv, medRxiv, ChemRxiv.
> Source: https://www.frontiersin.org/guidelines/policies-and-publication-ethics

**Current positioning (what the journal accepts now):** Human cognitive/social neuroscience across the lifespan (development, adulthood, aging): memory, attention, language, perception, sensory/multisensory processing, neuroimaging, psychophysiology, electrophysiology, consciousness, brain stimulation, motor/body representation. Recent (2026) Chinese-author papers seen in LetPub listing cover motor intervention therapy, brain stimulation, tai chi for pain relief, and neuromodulation techniques -- consistent with stated scope.

**Methods noted as welcome (qualitative — not a scored 0-5 table, see Methodological Preferences below):** neuroimaging (fMRI/EEG/MEG etc., implied by section scope), electrophysiology, psychophysiology, brain stimulation (TMS/tDCS-type), behavioral/cognitive experiments across developmental and aging populations, multisensory/sensory processing paradigms

### Reviewer Pool Characteristics

SciRev respondents rate reviewer-comment difficulty 3.7/5 ('difficult') and review-report quality 3.7/5, with overall manuscript-handling satisfaction only 3.0/5, based on an unspecified (unlabeled) small number of respondent reviews on SciRev -- treat as low-N. A Chinese aggregator (klxksci.com, could not be fetched directly to verify -- returned HTTP 403) is cited by a secondary source as saying reviewers are relatively professional with fast responses but have high English-language-quality expectations that can trigger language-polish requests; this specific claim could not be independently re-verified via direct fetch, so it is flagged as lower-confidence.
